answer: An AI market for vine health and lagoon data admits identity k only when a shared contract permanently locks k fixed-supply tokens. Its global issuance counter survives deletion, and collateral cannot back two identities. After n admissions, the next requires n+1 additional tokens; a farm’s n aliases therefore bind at least n(n+1)/2. Splitting wallets cannot reduce that sum. Pre-aging starts after escrow, with the entire bond locked through every pulse of activity.
